original_question: Consider a closed surface of genus ≥ 2 with a metric of non-positive curvature.
target_in_paper: Question 6.2.2 (Knieper) in §6.2, “Zero curvature geodesics and flat strips,” of the final arXiv version; the same problem appears in the submitted PDF as Question 6.5.1 in §6.5, “Closed geodesics.”
correct_elements: Your draft correctly identifies the precise geometric ambient setting of the target question: a closed surface of genus at least 2 equipped with a Riemannian metric of non-positive curvature.
missing_details: The paper’s question is a counting problem, not just a setup: one must define a function N(T).
N(T) counts free homotopy classes, not individual geodesics, flat strips, or points of the unit tangent bundle.
The counted classes are those containing a closed geodesic of length at most T along which the Gaussian curvature is identically zero.
The curvature condition is pointwise along the entire geodesic: the Gaussian curvature must be everywhere zero on that geodesic, not merely somewhere zero or zero on average.
The conclusion being asked for is a quadratic growth bound: does there exist a constant C > 0 such that N(T) ≤ C T^2?
To make the question stand alone, the quantifier on T should be explicit, e.g. for all T > 0.

The nearby context shows this question is weaker than the neighboring existence question for non-closed zero-curvature geodesics: the paper notes that a negative answer to Question 6.2.1 would imply N(T) is bounded.
If one follows the older submitted-PDF formulation (Question 6.5.1), there is an additional explicit hypothesis that N(T) grows subexponentially, namely lim_{T→∞} (log N(T))/T = 0.
refined_question: Let (M,g) be a closed Riemannian surface of genus at least 2 with Gaussian curvature K_g \le 0 everywhere. For T > 0, let N(T) be the number of free homotopy classes of loops in M that contain a closed g-geodesic of length at most T along which K_g vanishes identically. Must there exist a constant C > 0 such that N(T) \le C T^2 for all T > 0?
justification: The draft matches the opening hypothesis of Knieper’s question essentially verbatim, so the nearest paper-faithful target is the counting problem about zero-curvature closed geodesics, not the neighboring ergodicity question (Question 6.1.1) and not Burns’s existence question for a non-closed zero-curvature geodesic (Question 6.2.1). The nearby discussion explains why free homotopy classes and flat strips are the right objects and records that a negative answer to Question 6.2.1 would force boundedness of the counting function. There is also a version discrepancy worth noting: the final arXiv/html version presents the problem as Question 6.2.2, while the submitted PDF gives an explicit earlier formulation as Question 6.5.1, including the subexponential-growth hypothesis.
